page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.24xlarge is a high-capacity general purpose instance driven by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The physical compute foundation consists of an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz, delivering 48 physical cores and 96 virtual cores through simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is balanced at 384 GB of DDR4 RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. For localized input and output, the instance includes 3600 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD storage, while baseline network throughput reaches 100 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs are bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate substantial multi-core compute density, registering 81302.2 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a PassMark CPU score of 55532.59. Memory subsystems show strong transfer rates, reaching 4502.91 GB/sec on cached reads and over 215 GB/sec on large uncached blocks. Consequently, the instance excels in memory-dependent concurrent tasks, reaching 74.23 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and 44.21 GB/sec in static web serving. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects architectural limitations, with bottom-quartile ratings in single-core stress-ng and single-threaded gzip compression. LLM text generation throughput is similarly restrained, underscoring the lack of hardware accelerators.

The instance provides high resource density per deployment, combining enterprise-tier network capacity and local NVMe storage without requiring external volume attachments for temporary data. It presents an efficient profile for multi-threaded scale-up workloads, though users encounter diminishing returns on tasks dependent on clock-bound single-thread execution. The hardware profile aligns directly with high-throughput database systems, distributed caching layers, enterprise backend services, static content distribution, and extract-transform-load pipelines requiring high bandwidth and immediate local scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m5dn.24xlarge is a general purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores. Configured with a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, the system features 384 GB of DDR4 RAM and integrates 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reveal strong multi-core computation, high memory bandwidth, and high throughput in Redis SET operations and static web delivery. However, single-core metrics and single-threaded operations such as gzip compression demonstrate lower relative capability, and CPU-only LLM token generation is limited. Without hardware GPU accelerators, the instance is structurally cost-effective for dense multi-threaded services rather than single-threaded or deep learning training applications. The configuration is well suited for high-concurrency relational and NoSQL databases, in-memory caching systems, distributed data processing, and large-scale web application serving.
